newsitem.title: USA: Ferry to link Florida to Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Ferry to link Florida to Mexico.

text.p: Affluent Mexican and Central American shoppers will soon be able to hop on a ferry for a jaunt to the Florida city of Tampa.
Empress Cruise Lines said Friday it planned to launch regular ferry service from the Port of Tampa to the Yucatan Peninsula in February.
"It's the first road link between Mexico and Florida," said Espen Tandberg, marketing vice president of Empress, which is based in St. Petersburg.
The cruise company expects middle-class residents of Mexico, Costa Rica, Belize and other Central American nations to use the service for shopping trips.

"What Mexicans love to do is shop. But when they fly in, they are limited to two carry-on bags. On a ferry, they can buy refrigerators, TVs, microwave ovens and other items to take back home easily," he said.
Empress also expects a brisk business among American tour bus operators, who want to take groups to Mexico, he said.
"The NAFTA agreement has really helped this project along. American tour bus operators can drive their passengers right onto the ferry, and 27 hours later they arrive in the Yucatan," Tandberg said.

The ferry service will run four times a week, using the ships Seminole Empress and M.V. Mayan Empress. Each vessel is estimated to have an economic impact of $160 million each year on the state of Florida, he said.
An introductory offer will charge $550 for a family of four to take a car on the ferry, spend three nights at a beachfront hotel in Cancun, Mexico and return to Florida.
Empress said it chose the Port of Tampa for the Florida link, but it is still in negotiations with Mexico's Puerto Progreso and Puerto Calica to finalise the Cancun link.
